Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $g(K)$ be the least genus of a compact connected oriented embedded surface in $S^3$ with boundary $K$. With the integral Alexander normalization, the maximum Alexander grading in which the hat knot Floer homology of $K$ is nonzero is $g(K)$:

$$g(K)=\max\{i\in\mathbb Z:\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^3,K,i;\mathbb Z)\ne0\}.$$
F6: [F6] [[lem-countable-analytic-choice-for-fixed-sutured-floer-data]] supplies the Countable Choice selection branch for the actual local analytic constructions used in F2–F4 on the fixed finite diagram/cut hierarchy. The pointwise Fredholm parametrices, domain-area bounds, protected-divisor barriers, finite-dimensional Sard reductions and local gluing constructions are those already constructed at these actual targets. Their choices are made on countable separable chart covers as specified in F6; the proof does not invoke the broader full-Choice existence declaration as an assumption. The geometric hierarchy and its finite diagram words are chosen for this one manifold and have only finitely many stages.
Proof2.1: 2.1 Apply the restricted branch F6 to the fixed finite hierarchy and its diagram choices: the integer domain classes, required finite parameter families, separable Sobolev/perturbation spaces and protected neighborhoods are exactly the inputs described there. This makes the simultaneous regular data, compactness extractions, gluing charts and determinant selections under Countable Choice. With these choices, apply the actual construction F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g. [F3, F4, F6, step 1.3]
